meta.titre: Uses of Non-Metals: from air and sulphur to fertilisers and acids

sections.contenu_markdown: A farmer in Buea spreads a bag of fertiliser on his maize field, a pharmacist in Douala uses sulphur ointment, and a welder at Bonaberi uses oxygen to cut steel. All of these depend on non-metallic elements and their compounds. Nitrogen from the air becomes fertiliser, sulphur becomes the acid in car batteries, and carbon appears as diamond, graphite and charcoal. The GCE O/L paper often asks for a large-scale use of a named non-metal or compound, so you must link each substance to its property and its main use.

items: Air contains about 78 % nitrogen and 21 % oxygen.
Carbon exists as diamond, graphite and amorphous forms such as charcoal.
Fertilisers supply the elements nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium needed by plants.

sections.titre: Main uses of non-metals and their compounds
sections.contenu_markdown:
A use always follows from a **property**. Learn each use together with the property that explains it.

| Substance | Property | Main uses |
|---|---|---|
| Nitrogen | unreactive; very cold when liquid | manufacture of ammonia; inert gas in food packaging; liquid nitrogen as a coolant |
| Ammonia | reacts with acids to give ammonium salts | manufacture of **fertilisers** (ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate, urea) and nitric acid; cleaning products |
| Sulphur | burns to sulphur dioxide | manufacture of sulphuric acid; vulcanising rubber; matches |
| Sulphur dioxide | bleaches; kills bacteria | bleaching wood pulp; preserving dried fruit; making sulphuric acid |
| Sulphur trioxide | reacts with water to give acid | manufacture of **sulphuric acid** |
| Oxygen | supports combustion and respiration | breathing in hospitals; welding and cutting metals; making steel |
| Hydrogen | very light; burns | making ammonia; hardening vegetable oils into margarine; rocket fuel |
| Carbon (graphite) | soft, conducts electricity | pencils, lubricant, electrodes |
| Carbon (diamond) | very hard | cutting and drilling tools; jewellery |
| Carbon (charcoal, coke) | burns; absorbs colour | fuel; removing colour and smells; coke reduces iron ore |
| Carbon dioxide | does not burn; dissolves in water | fizzy drinks; fire extinguishers; solid CO$_2$ as a coolant |
| Chlorine | kills germs; bleaches | purifying water; making bleach and PVC |
| Helium, neon, argon | unreactive | helium in balloons; neon in signs; argon in light bulbs |

variantes.nom: The two industrial processes in outline
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked about ammonia or sulphuric acid manufacture.
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Haber process:** nitrogen and hydrogen react over an iron catalyst at about 450 $^\circ$C and high pressure, $\mathrm{N_{2}} + 3\mathrm{H_{2}} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH_{3}}$. **Contact process:** sulphur burns to give sulphur dioxide, $\mathrm{S} + \mathrm{O_{2}} \rightarrow \mathrm{SO_{2}}$; sulphur dioxide is oxidised over vanadium(V) oxide at about 450 $^\circ$C, $2\mathrm{SO_{2}} + \mathrm{O_{2}} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO_{3}}$; sulphur trioxide is absorbed in concentrated sulphuric acid, $\mathrm{SO_{3}} + \mathrm{H_{2}SO_{4}} \rightarrow \mathrm{H_{2}S_{2}O_{7}}$, and the product is diluted, $\mathrm{H_{2}S_{2}O_{7}} + \mathrm{H_{2}O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H_{2}SO_{4}}$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When fertilisers are compared or made.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ammonia is neutralised with acids: $\mathrm{NH_{3}} + \mathrm{HNO_{3}} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH_{4}NO_{3}}$ and $2\mathrm{NH_{3}} + \mathrm{H_{2}SO_{4}} \rightarrow \mathrm{(NH_{4})_{2}SO_{4}}$. A better fertiliser has a higher percentage of nitrogen by mass: ammonium nitrate $\dfrac{28}{80} = 35\ \%$, ammonium sulphate $\dfrac{28}{132} = 21.2\ \%$, urea $\dfrac{28}{60} = 46.7\ \%$. Too much fertiliser washed into rivers pollutes the water.

sections.enonce_markdown: A farmer compares two fertilisers sold in 50 kg bags. Urea, $\mathrm{CO(NH_{2})_{2}}$, costs $20\,000$ FCFA per bag and ammonium sulphate, $\mathrm{(NH_{4})_{2}SO_{4}}$, costs $14\,000$ FCFA per bag. ($A_r$: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32.) (a) Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in each. (b) Calculate the mass of nitrogen in each bag. (c) Which fertiliser is cheaper per kilogram of nitrogen, and by how much?

etapes.justification: Add the atomic masses of all atoms in the formula.
Percentage $= \dfrac{\text{mass of N in one formula}}{M_r} \times 100$; both formulas contain 2 N atoms, $2 \times 14 = 28$.

etapes.action: Find the mass of nitrogen in a 50 kg bag.
Find the cost per kilogram of nitrogen.
etapes.justification: Cost per kg of N = price of the bag divided by the mass of N in the bag.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Urea: $\dfrac{20\,000}{23.3} = 857$ FCFA per kg. Ammonium sulphate: $\dfrac{14\,000}{10.6} = 1\,320$ FCFA per kg.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Urea contains $46.7\ \%$ nitrogen against $21.2\ \%$ for ammonium sulphate, and it is cheaper per kilogram of nitrogen: about $857$ FCFA against $1\,320$ FCFA, although the bag costs more.

items.erreur_markdown: "Nitrogen is used to make things burn faster."
items.pourquoi_faux: Nitrogen does not support combustion. It is unreactive, which is why it is used as an inert gas to protect food.
items.correction_markdown: Oxygen supports burning; nitrogen is used for ammonia manufacture and as an inert atmosphere.

items.erreur_markdown: "Sulphur burns in air to form sulphur trioxide, which gives sulphuric acid directly."
items.pourquoi_faux: Burning sulphur gives sulphur dioxide. It must be oxidised further over a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst to give sulphur trioxide.

items.erreur_markdown: "Diamond is used as a lubricant because it is very smooth."
items.pourquoi_faux: Diamond is very hard and is used for cutting. Graphite is the soft form of carbon with layers that slide, used as a lubricant.
items.correction_markdown: Diamond: cutting tools and jewellery. Graphite: lubricant, pencils and electrodes.

items.erreur_markdown: "Carbon dioxide extinguishers work by supplying oxygen to the fire."
items.pourquoi_faux: Carbon dioxide does not burn and does not support burning. It covers the fire and keeps oxygen away.
items.correction_markdown: Carbon dioxide puts out fires by excluding oxygen.

items.erreur_markdown: "The best fertiliser is the one with the biggest formula mass."
items.pourquoi_faux: What matters for a nitrogen fertiliser is the percentage of nitrogen by mass, not the formula mass.
items.correction_markdown: Urea has a small formula mass (60) but a high nitrogen percentage ($46.7\ \%$).

items.enonce_markdown: Complete each sentence with the correct substance and its property. (a) ........ is used for welding and cutting metals because it supports combustion. (b) ........ is used to fill electric light bulbs because it is unreactive. (c) ........ is added to drinking water to kill germs. (d) ........ is used to make fizzy drinks. (Choose from: chlorine, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide.)
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Oxygen**. (b) **Argon**. (c) **Chlorine**. (d) **Carbon dioxide** (it dissolves in water under pressure).

items.enonce_markdown: Ammonium sulphate is made by neutralising sulphuric acid with ammonia: $2\mathrm{NH_{3}} + \mathrm{H_{2}SO_{4}} \rightarrow \mathrm{(NH_{4})_{2}SO_{4}}$. ($A_r$: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32.) (a) Calculate the relative formula mass of ammonium sulphate. (b) What mass of ammonia is needed to make 66 kg of ammonium sulphate? (c) Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in ammonium sulphate.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $2 \times (14 + 4) + 32 + 64 = $ **132**.

(b) $66\ \mathrm{kg} \div 132 = 0.50\ \mathrm{kmol}$ of ammonium sulphate. From the equation, 1 mol of salt needs 2 mol of $\mathrm{NH_3}$, so $0.50 \times 2 = 1.0\ \mathrm{kmol}$ of ammonia. $M(\mathrm{NH_3}) = 17$, so mass $= 1.0 \times 17 = $ **17 kg**.

(c) $\dfrac{28}{132} \times 100 = $ **21.2 %**.

items.enonce_markdown: In the contact process sulphur is converted to sulphuric acid: $\mathrm{S} + \mathrm{O_{2}} \rightarrow \mathrm{SO_{2}}$, $2\mathrm{SO_{2}} + \mathrm{O_{2}} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO_{3}}$ and $\mathrm{SO_{3}} + \mathrm{H_{2}O} \rightarrow \mathrm{H_{2}SO_{4}}$. ($A_r$: H = 1, O = 16, S = 32.) (a) State one large-scale use of sulphuric acid and one large-scale use of sulphur dioxide. (b) Name the catalyst used in the second reaction. (c) Calculate the maximum mass of sulphuric acid that can be made from 16 kg of sulphur. (d) If the process has an overall yield of 90 %, what mass of acid is actually obtained?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Sulphuric acid: manufacture of fertilisers (ammonium sulphate), or car batteries, detergents, paints. Sulphur dioxide: bleaching wood pulp, preserving food, or making sulphuric acid.

(b) **Vanadium(V) oxide**.

(c) One mole of sulphur gives one mole of sulphuric acid through the three steps (ratio 1 : 1 : 1 : 1). $n(\mathrm{S}) = \dfrac{16}{32} = 0.50\ \mathrm{kmol}$; $M(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}) = 98$. Mass $= 0.50 \times 98 = $ **49 kg**.

(d) $49 \times \dfrac{90}{100} = $ **44.1 kg**.

items_markdown: Link every use to a property: unreactive nitrogen and argon protect food and filament lamps, hard diamond cuts, soft graphite lubricates.
Large-scale uses: nitrogen for making ammonia; ammonia for fertilisers; sulphur trioxide for making sulphuric acid.
Ammonia is made by the Haber process (iron catalyst); sulphuric acid by the contact process (vanadium(V) oxide catalyst).
Compare fertilisers by the percentage of nitrogen by mass; urea $46.7\ \%$, ammonium nitrate $35\ \%$, ammonium sulphate $21.2\ \%$.
Oxygen supports combustion and respiration; carbon dioxide extinguishes fires and makes drinks fizzy; chlorine kills germs in water.
